title: Zakariyya: don't leave me alone
hookLine: my Lord, don't leave me alone, and You are the best of inheritors (21:89)
last: HARM TOUCHED ME; YOU ARE MERCIFUL.

lines: AN OLD MAN IN THE SANCTUARY.
cards: An old man prays in the sanctuary. His bones have grown weak, he says, and his head is ablaze with white hair. His wife is barren.
He has been looking after a girl named Maryam, and whenever he goes in to her he finds food with her, and she tells him it is from God. And there, watching her, he speaks.
Surah Maryam says he called to his Lord with a hidden call, a prayer said low, almost in secret. Today, Zakariyya.

teach.b: Al-Anbiya gives his prayer in one verse. Pickthall: "My Lord! Leave me not childless, though Thou art the best of inheritors." The Arabic is la tadharni fardan.

Fard means single, one alone, so the plainest sense is: don't leave me alone. Pickthall renders it childless, and that is the sense: no son, no one to carry on the work after him. But the word underneath is lonelier.
Then the second half: You are the best of inheritors. In the same breath that he asks for an heir, he admits that God inherits everything in the end anyway. He's asking and letting go at once.
Ayyub, yesterday, named his pain and God's mercy. Zakariyya names his fear and God's lasting. The next verse says: so We answered him, and gave him Yahya, and made his wife fit for him.
The Qur'an doesn't stop at the family. It says these prophets used to hurry toward good deeds, and called on God in longing and in fear, and were humble before Him.

In Surah Maryam, he asks for a sign that it's real, and is told he will not speak to people for three nights, though he is well. So the man whose prayer was a whisper gets an answer he has to carry in silence.

Commentators point out where the prayer started: watching Maryam, a young girl provided for in ways no one could explain. Seeing God give to someone else is what made him brave enough to ask for himself.

how: Many Muslims recite Zakariyya's prayer from 21:89 when hoping for children, and some use it more widely when asking not to be left alone; it is said quietly, as a personal supplication.

o: the old man who prayed low not to be left alone
the guardian of the Ka'ba in Ibrahim's time
the young prophet born to an elderly couple

games.q: inside Zakariyya's prayer — tap the pairs.
p: God inherits everything in the end
the sign: he would not speak

s: Zakariyya's prayer in Surah Maryam is a shout in the temple
it calls his prayer a secret, said in a low voice.
la tadharni fardan means, at root, don't leave me single, alone
Pickthall renders it childless, which is what he meant; the word fard means one alone.
the Qur'an says Zakariyya never asked for a sign
in Surah Maryam he asks for one, and is told he won't speak to people for three nights.

games.q: you're old, and God has just told you you'll have a son. what do you ask next?
o: nothing. you just say thank you.
for the child to be born soon.
games.why: he asks for a sign, and the sign is silence: three nights without speaking to people, though he is well.

practice: Notice whether there's a loneliness you've stopped mentioning, even to yourself: a friend you lost touch with, a home that's too quiet, a hope set down years ago; or think of someone else who is alone right now.
If you pray, you can use Zakariyya's words, my Lord, don't leave me alone, for yourself or for them. If you don't, just hold that person in mind for a while.

wordCard.voice: Zakariyya. The old servant of the sanctuary who asked, in secret, not to be left alone, and was given Yahya. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Zakariyya, known in the Bible as Zechariah, father of Yahya (John).

carryVoice: Your line: don't leave me alone. A prayer can ask and let go in the same breath. A week, done.

sources.q: My Lord! Leave me not childless, though Thou art the best of inheritors.
